handoff.purpose: Annotation parsing and normalization utilities (expression parsing, de-stringifying, member collection, union flattening).

symbols.name: _ANN_DEPTH
symbols.note: Maximum recursion depth for annotation processing (16).

symbols.name: _STMT_DEPTH
symbols.note: Maximum recursion depth for statement processing (64).

symbols.name: _parse_expr
symbols.note: Parse one expression string using ast.parse(mode='eval'), returns AST node or None; never raises.

symbols.name: _dotted_tail
symbols.note: Extracts the tail identifier from a Name or Attribute node.

symbols.name: _nominal_text
symbols.note: Returns the name as written for an edge, using ast.unparse fallback.

symbols.name: _slice_elements
symbols.note: Extracts elements from a slice (Tuple or Index) as a list.

symbols.name: _destring
symbols.note: Recursively replaces forward-reference string constants with parsed expressions; avoids Literal and Annotated metadata.

symbols.name: annotation_text
symbols.note: Returns canonicalized annotation text from an AST node, using deep copy and de-stringifying.

symbols.name: _AnnAcc
symbols.note: Accumulator for annotation members, containers, dropped names, and flags (None, Any, Union, unparsed).

symbols.name: _gather_dropped
symbols.note: Collects nominal names discarded by element rules (mapping keys, Callable parameters).

symbols.name: _collect
symbols.note: Recursively collects annotation members, containers, and flags from an AST node.

symbols.name: normalize_annotation
symbols.note: Reads one raw annotation string and returns an Annotation object with parsed members/containers/flags.

symbols.name: flatten_union
symbols.note: Flattens union types (including Optional, Union, |) into a tuple of raw texts, removing None.

claims.text: Two places are deliberately left alone: ``Literal["a"]``, whose strings are VALUES and would become a type called ``a``, and every ``Annotated[...]`` argument after the first, which is metadata and not a type at all.

claims.text: ``Optional[Alpha]`` -> ``("Alpha",)``; ``Alpha | None`` -> ``("Alpha",)``; ``Union[Alpha, Beta]`` -> ``("Alpha", "Beta")``. A non-union annotation is its own single member, so the caller needs no special case. Nesting does not multiply members: ``Optional[Union[A, B]]`` is still two.

observations.what: _destring does not copy the node before mutation; relies on caller to copy.
_slice_elements uses getattr for ast.Index which is removed in Python 3.9+; will raise AttributeError if used.
normalize_annotation uses lru_cache with maxsize=8192; fine for typical usage.
flatten_union is truncated; the walk function is defined but the rest of the function is missing.
